reference_title: UFC 4-023-03, Design of Buildings to Resist Progressive Collapse (DoD, dated 14 July 2009, as amended through Change 4, 10 June 2024)

sections.title: Chapter Overview
sections.summary: Material-specific cold-formed-steel requirements; Appendix G demonstrates them on a load-bearing wall building. Composite portions use the other applicable material chapter.
sections.body: This chapter provides the specific requirements for designing a cold-formed steel building to resist progressive collapse. If composite construction with other materials is employed, use the design guidance from the appropriate material chapter for those elements/portions. Note that the combination of design requirements (TF, AP, and ELR) will depend upon the Risk Category of the building, as defined in Section 2-2.
key_points: The shortest material chapter; follows the same structure as Chapters 6-7

sections.title: Material Properties for Cold-Formed Steel
sections.summary: ASCE 41 provides default expected-strength values for light-metal-framing shear walls; when a default LOWER-bound value is needed, multiply the expected-strength value by 0.85 -- the same rule and factor as wood (Section 7-1).
sections.body: ASCE 41 provides default expected strength values for light metal framing shear walls. When default lower bound strength values are needed, multiply the expected strength values by 0.85.
key_points: Lower-bound = 0.85 x expected strength (same rule as wood, Section 7-1)
sections.applicability: Feeds QCE/QCL determination for cold-formed steel Tie Force and Alternate Path calculations.

sections.title: Strength Reduction Factor Phi for Cold-Formed Steel
sections.summary: Phi comes from the AISI/COS/NASPEC North American Specification for the Design of Cold-Formed Steel Structural Members.
sections.body: For Tie Force and Alternate Path methods, use the appropriate strength reduction factor specified in AISI/COS/NASPEC AISI Standard North American Specification for the Design of Cold-Formed Steel Structural Members for the component and behavior under consideration. If cold formed steel components can be proven capable of carrying the required tie strengths while undergoing 0.20-rad rotation, use the appropriate Phi for each limit state considered.
key_points: Phi source: AISI/COS/NASPEC North American Specification
sections.applicability: General Phi-factor pointer for cold-formed steel.

sections.title: Tie Force Requirements for Cold-Formed Steel
sections.summary: Apply Section 3-1 for load-bearing cold-formed steel buildings.
sections.body: Apply the Tie Force requirements in Section 3-1, where applicable, for load-bearing cold-formed steel buildings.

sections.title: Alternate Path Method for Cold-Formed Steel
sections.summary: General procedure per Section 3-2 (8-4.1); modeling/acceptance criteria are the ASCE 41 Chapter 12 Life-Safety values, unmodified by this UFC (8-4.2) -- identical structure to wood's Chapter 12 pointer.
sections.body: General (8-4.1): use the Alternate Path method in Section 3-2, where applicable, to verify that the structure can bridge over removed elements. Modeling and Acceptance Criteria (8-4.2): use the modeling parameters, nonlinear acceptance criteria and linear m-factors for the Life Safety condition from ASCE 41 Chapter 12 for primary and secondary components; use ASCE 41's modeling parameters and guidance for the analytical model.
key_points: No UFC-specific replacement tables -- ASCE 41 Chapter 12 Life-Safety values apply directly (same source chapter as wood)
sections.applicability: The cold-formed-steel-specific application of the general Alternate Path method, validated by Appendix G.

sections.title: Enhanced Local Resistance Requirements for Cold-Formed Steel
sections.summary: Apply Section 3-3's material-independent ELR procedure to framed and load-bearing wall cold-formed steel buildings.
sections.body: Apply the Enhanced Local Resistance requirements in Section 3-3, where applicable, for framed and load-bearing wall cold-formed steel buildings.
key_points: ELR for cold-formed steel: pure pointer to Section 3-3
